title: THE SOCIOLINGUISTIC FOUNDATIONS OF LANGUAGE MODELING

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical framework and conceptual analysis proposing that language models inherently model specific 'varieties of language.' It analyzes how the underrepresentation of certain dialects and registers in training corpora leads to quality-of-service harms and stereotyping, and proposes stratified corpus design as a mitigation strategy rather than empirical benchmarking.

bias_targets.target: Social and Demographic bias (Gender, Race, Ethnicity)
bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual discussion explaining how semantic and selection biases against specific social groups (e.g., ethnicities and genders) manifest in language models as a direct result of varietal misalignment and the lack of sociolinguistic diversity in uncurated training data.
